title: Imports and Setup
content: The formalization imports the full Mathlib library, bringing in topological spaces, homeomorphisms, cardinal arithmetic, and set operations. The `open Set Cardinal` command puts set and cardinal notations in scope. The variable `{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]` establishes a generic topological space for the definitions.
mathContext: We work in a general topological space $(X, \tau)$ with Mathlib's `TopologicalSpace` typeclass, later specialized to $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ for the concrete conjectures.

title: Connected Subsets Collection
content: Defines `connectedSubsetsOf S` as the set of all connected subsets contained in $S$. A subset $T \subseteq S$ is in this collection iff $T \subseteq S$ and $T$ is connected (cannot be partitioned into two disjoint non-empty open sets in the subspace topology).
mathContext: $\text{connectedSubsetsOf}(S) = \{T \subseteq S : T \text{ is connected}\}$. A set $T$ is connected iff there is no decomposition $T = U \cup V$ with $U, V$ open, non-empty, and disjoint.

title: Homeomorphism Between Subsets
content: Defines `AreHomeomorphic S T` as the existence of a homeomorphism $S \simeq_t T$ — a continuous bijection with continuous inverse, where $S$ and $T$ carry the subspace topology. This captures topological equivalence: $S$ and $T$ have identical topological structure.
mathContext: $\text{AreHomeomorphic}(S, T) :\iff \exists f: S \to T$ continuous bijection with $f^{-1}$ continuous, i.e., $S \cong T$ as topological spaces. Formally: $\text{Nonempty}(S \simeq_t T)$.

title: Diverse Connected Subset
content: A set $S$ has a diverse connected subset if there exists $T \subsetneq S$ that is: (1) connected, (2) contains at least two points (not a singleton), and (3) not homeomorphic to $S$. This formalizes Erdos's intuition that connected sets should possess 'intermediate' connected substructures that are topologically distinct from the whole.
mathContext: $\text{HasDiverseConnectedSubset}(S) :\iff \exists T \subsetneq S,\; T \text{ connected} \wedge |T| \geq 2 \wedge T \not\cong S$.

title: Rudin Set
content: A set $S$ is a Rudin set if it is connected and every proper connected subset is either a singleton $\{x\}$ or homeomorphic to $S$ itself. This extreme self-similarity means the topology of $S$ is maximally rigid: there are no 'intermediate' connected substructures. The `ExistsUnique` formulation ensures each singleton is identified by a unique point.
mathContext: $\text{IsRudinSet}(S) :\iff S \text{ connected} \wedge \forall T \subsetneq S,\; T \text{ connected} \implies (\exists! x,\; T = \{x\}) \vee T \cong S$.

title: Homeomorphism Reflexivity
content: Every set is homeomorphic to itself, via the identity homeomorphism `Homeomorph.refl S`. This is a basic property of the homeomorphism relation.

title: Homeomorphism Symmetry
content: If $S \cong T$ then $T \cong S$: homeomorphism is symmetric. The proof uses `Homeomorph.symm` to invert the continuous bijection.

title: Erdos's First Conjecture (Disproved)
content: States that every connected set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ has a diverse connected subset: a proper connected non-singleton subset not homeomorphic to the whole. Erdos posed this in the 1940s, expecting an affirmative answer based on the behavior of typical connected sets like intervals and disks. Disproved by Rudin (1958) under CH.

title: Connected Subset Cardinality and Second Conjecture
content: Defines `connectedSubsetCardinality S` as the cardinal $|\text{connectedSubsetsOf}(S)|$ and `erdosSecondConjecture`: every connected set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ has strictly more than $2^{\aleph_0}$ connected subsets. For typical connected sets (intervals, manifolds), the number of connected subsets is indeed $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$, but the Rudin set achieves exactly $2^{\aleph_0}$.

title: Rudin's Theorem (1958) — Axiomatized
content: The central axiom: under the Continuum Hypothesis ($\aleph_1 = 2^{\aleph_0}$), there exists a connected subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is a Rudin set with exactly $2^{\aleph_0}$ connected subsets and is nontrivial ($|S| \geq 2$). Mary Ellen Rudin's construction uses transfinite induction of length $\aleph_1$ (which equals $2^{\aleph_0}$ under CH) to build $S$ point by point while maintaining both connectivity and the self-similarity property at each successor stage. This was published in 'A connected subset of the plane' (Fundamenta Mathematicae 46, 1958).

title: Rudin Sets Have No Diverse Subsets
content: The key structural theorem, fully proved (no sorry): for any Rudin set $S$, $\neg\text{HasDiverseConnectedSubset}(S)$. The proof assumes a diverse subset $T$ exists, then applies the Rudin property: since $T$ is a proper connected non-singleton subset of $S$, it must be either a singleton (contradicting $|T| \geq 2$) or homeomorphic to $S$ (contradicting $T \not\cong S$). Both cases lead to contradiction.
mathContext: $\text{IsRudinSet}(S) \implies \neg\text{HasDiverseConnectedSubset}(S)$. Proof by contradiction: if $T$ is diverse, then $T \subsetneq S$, $T$ connected, $|T| \geq 2$, $T \not\cong S$. But the Rudin property gives $T = \{x\}$ or $T \cong S$, both contradictions.

title: First Conjecture False Under CH
content: Proves $\text{CH} \to \neg\text{erdosFirstConjecture}$, fully verified (0 sorries). The proof: assume CH, obtain the Rudin set $S$ from the axiom, apply the first conjecture to $S$ to get a diverse subset, then apply `rudin_set_no_diverse_subset` to derive a contradiction.

title: Second Conjecture False Under CH
content: Proves $\text{CH} \to \neg\text{erdosSecondConjecture}$, fully verified (0 sorries). The proof: the Rudin set has exactly $2^{\aleph_0}$ connected subsets, but the conjecture requires strictly more than $2^{\aleph_0}$. Substituting the cardinality bound yields $2^{\aleph_0} > 2^{\aleph_0}$, a contradiction via `lt_irrefl`.
mathContext: $\text{CH} \implies \neg(\forall S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,\; S \text{ connected} \implies |\text{connectedSubsetsOf}(S)| > 2^{\aleph_0})$. The Rudin set achieves exactly $2^{\aleph_0}$, so $2^{\aleph_0} > 2^{\aleph_0}$ is absurd.

title: Both Conjectures False Under CH
content: The combined summary theorem: under CH, both of Erdos's conjectures about connected subsets of Euclidean space are false. Constructed as a simple conjunction of the two individual disproof theorems. This is the main exported result of the formalization.
